1.title: Push power wires into board
1.say: Push the thin white wire into the top left hole of the white board. Push the thin blue wire into the top right hole of the white board.
placements: thin white power wire from battery pack → top edge hole on left side of white plug board in its own cross row of five holes, pushed down firmly with fingers; in the video: upper left, numbers not readable so match picture

thin blue power wire from battery pack → top edge hole on right side of white plug board in its own cross row of five holes, pushed down firmly with fingers; in the video: upper right, numbers not readable so match picture
watch_for: If both wires sit in the same cross row the battery is shorted, so move one wire to a different row with empty board between.
If a wire feels loose or falls out it is not deep enough, so push it straight down until the bare metal disappears.
1.check_yourself: It should look like the white board sitting flat with a thin white wire sticking straight up on the left top and a thin blue wire sticking straight up on the right top.

2.title: Put the resistor across board
2.say: Push one thin leg of the small blue resistor into the white wire row. Push the other thin leg into an empty middle row.
placements: small blue striped resistor with two thin bent wire legs → left leg in same five hole row as thin white power wire on left top, right leg in empty five hole row toward middle to meet later short leg of light, body arched flat just above board, pushed with fingers; in the video: lying across top of white board, exact holes not readable so match picture
watch_for: If both legs sit in the same five hole row the part does nothing, so check that left and right legs are in different rows.
If the tiny tube wobbles or pops up one leg is shallow, so push each leg straight down until snug.
2.check_yourself: It should look like a tiny blue striped tube lying flat above the white board with a thin wire arching down on the left near the white wire and on the right near the middle.

3.title: Plug in the blue LED
3.say: Hold the small blue dome light so the short leg is on the left. Push the short leg into the resistor middle row. Push the long leg into the blue wire row.
placements: small blue dome light with one long leg for plus side and one short leg with flat side for minus side → short leg in same five hole row as right leg of resistor in middle, long leg in same five hole row as thin blue power wire on right top, dome standing straight up, pushed with fingers; in the video: upright on right side of white board glowing blue, exact holes not readable so match picture
watch_for: If the blue dome stays dark the legs are likely swapped, so switch the long leg with the short leg rows.
If both legs share the same five hole row the light is shorted and stays dark, so move each leg to its own row described above.
3.check_yourself: It should look like a small blue dome standing straight up on the right side of the white board glowing bright blue with the resistor lying flat to its left.
